extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, judges, and advanced law students (practitioners handling preliminary injunctions in patent cases)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural guidance for seeking, opposing, and framing preliminary (and ex parte) injunctions in patent-infringement litigation, including who may be enjoined, required allegations and evidence, hearing practice, scope and duration of orders, and bonding conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee liability and scope of injunction against licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: The licensee owner is liable to the other owners from selling within his territory like any other infringer; an injunction will be granted against a licensee unless his acts are in accordance with his license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensee who transcends his rights may be enjoined. A licensee who uses the patent without paying his license fees may be enjoined whether the license is voidable or not. The partner of a licensee enjoys the immunity bestowed on his copartner while the firm fulfills its obligations to the licensor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vendee's rights when purchased article infringes vendor's other patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A vendee may use the article purchased though it infringes another patent of the vendor, if it cannot otherwise be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case example: Roosevelt v. Westem Electric Co. (1884). This is an exception to immediate enjoinability of purchasers; context and possible alternatives affect relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-owner licensee vs. other co-owner's suit
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee under one co-owner of the patent will not be enjoined at the suit of the other co-owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Clum v. Brewer (1866). Rights among co-owners and their licensees can limit availability of injunctive relief by a co-owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successor/assignee taking after injunction with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A new party, taking under an infringer after injunction with notice, has the same rights in reference to the plaintiff as his vendor, and is not an independent infringer, but is liable once to be enjoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a transferee cannot give a bond instead of being enjoined; the transferee's previous knowledge and timing are material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of agents and principals
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant who proclaims himself to be the agent of another will be treated as a principal if the infringing article bears his name and other evidence points to him as primarily responsible, and as such he will be enjoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actual agents who sell infringing articles on behalf of their maker or owner are liable to injunction, even if they have no interest in the vended articles or proceeds. A salesman making a separate profit may be enjoined even though his employer is sued in another district.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons furnishing tools/materials — remoteness of liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether those who contribute to the infringing act by furnishing tools and materials therefor, in the due course of business and without participation in the act or its direct results, can be enjoined is doubtful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On principle their connection appears too remote to warrant an injunction; active participation or direct responsibility is required for injunctive relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: No injunction where defendant ceased infringing before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: No injunction can be granted against a defendant whose interest in the infringing enterprise had expired before the filing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption of intent to infringe arising from past infringements ceases when defendant no longer capable of violating plaintiff's rights. Where infringer dies, personal representatives cannot be enjoined until they manifest intent to continue infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of application for preliminary injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be incorporated into the original bill or constitute a separate proceeding; in any case it must clearly state the plaintiff's right and its intended violation by the defendant, and pray for immediate interference of the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must set forth production of the invention by patentee or assignor, issue of the patent, title of plaintiff, that plaintiff has practised the invention and enjoys his exclusive privilege (except as to defendant), and should allege judgments, public acquiescence, or equivalent facts supporting presumption of right. If independent, the application must be complete and disclose all matters the court must pass on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of alleged infringing acts in application/motion
rubrics_metrics.description: The application (or motion) must set out the particular acts intended to be an infringement so that the court may judge whether they are invasions of the patent; general allegations are not sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion for preliminary injunction should set out the acts constituting the infringement; failure to do so may render motion insufficient (see Kirby Bung Mfg. Co. v. White (1880)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Averments when patent expired or alleged infringing articles made during term
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent has expired, it must be averred that the alleged infringing articles were made during the term of the patent and in violation of its provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking to enjoin post-expiration acts, plaintiff must show manufacture/violation during patent term to justify equitable relief concerning those articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath and truthfulness requirements on application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be supported by the oath of the plaintiff, who must also swear that he or his assignor is the original inventor of the art or instrument protected by the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False swearing in an affidavit used on motion for an injunction is perjury; courts take oath requirements seriously (see Baldwin v. Bernard (1872)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and ex parte practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically Federal courts required notice and hearing before injunctions; since the act of 1874 courts have been interpreted to have authority to grant ex parte injunctions in equity, though whether complete departure from prior principle will be sustained is doubtful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where notice is required it must be reasonable, but can be waived by appearance. In cases of great emergency temporary restraining orders could be granted pending application. Courts accept affidavits and proofs on both sides where notice is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer requirements to application for injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: The answer to an application for an injunction is subject to the same general rules as an answer to an original bill: it confesses whatever it does not deny; where denial involves validity the answer must set forth particular facts on which the denial rests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the defendant appears he may admit, traverse, or avoid averments; failure to appear allows ex parte hearing on plaintiff's evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material questions to be considered on the injunction hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Material questions include: the nature of the invention; the standing of the plaintiff in the trade; the character and extent of the infringement; whether the defendant makes and sells or only uses the invention; the responsibility of the defendant for damages and profits; and the inconvenience to the respective parties of denying or allowing the injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court weighs these factors in determining whether summary relief is appropriate; some matters (e.g., a plaintiff's inability to use invention because of prior patents) may be immaterial in the injunction inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence presentation and affidavit practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence on the hearing is presented by affidavits: plaintiff's affidavits usually with the application, defendant's with the answer, plaintiff closes in rebutter; each party allowed reasonable time to inspect the other's affidavits; evidence not submitted to inspection cannot be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits filed after stipulated dates ordinarily cannot be considered; affidavits on both sides may be read as to controversies in the bill. Practice allows some latitude in temporary injunction proceedings, but fairness and opportunity to inspect are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper classes of evidence to support an injunction motion
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion for an injunction may be supported by the following classes of evidence: (1) Letters-Patent; (2) Renewal of Patent; (3) Recovery in Equity; (4) Recovery at Law; (5) Possession and use; (6) Special injunctions against other parties; (7) Special injunctions against the present defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also admissible: judgments sustaining the patent, public acquiescence, written instruments proving title, expert testimony, and personal inspection by court as needed to show identity of defendant's device with the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte hearing burden and presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the hearing proceeds ex parte because defendant fails to appear, if plaintiff's affidavits show the issue of the patent and a judgment in its favor or public acquiescence, and a probable infringement by defendant, an injunction will issue though the court may have some doubt about validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, however, the patent is defective on its face or the plaintiff's title is uncertain, an injunction will be refused. The plaintiff's affidavits must make a prima facie showing in ex parte contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden when opposing evidence presented
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application is heard upon opposing evidence and the plaintiff's affidavits make a prima facie case for an injunction, the defendant must present testimony sufficient to overcome the presumptions thus created or prove circumstances rendering the allowance of an injunction inexpedient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court decides on broad equitable views and generally will not decide difficult or finely balanced legal questions at the preliminary stage; conflicting evidence may be sent to a jury or master for further fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's equitable discretion and scope of inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The application will be decided on broad views of the equitable rights of the parties; the court can examine only far enough to ascertain whether the plaintiff has an apparent title to protection and cannot enter into inquiries concerning difficult questions of law or the weight and value of conflicting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies granting provisional relief even where substantial legal disputes remain, provided equity as a whole favors protection and plaintiff has apparent title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and tailoring of preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary injunction may contain a general or a limited prohibition, and may issue either alone or in connection with other special orders for relief; when certain claims are disputed, the injunction may be confined to those unquestionably valid; where certain infringing articles cannot be equitably enjoined he may be forbidden to procure others and employ them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Injunctions should be fitted to each case to protect the plaintiff without unnecessary injury to the defendant; courts may couple injunctions with orders for a bond, an account, or other terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional injunctions and bond/indemnity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where doubt exists, the plaintiff may be compelled to secure the defendant against the injury caused by the injunction by a bond of indemnity payable if the injunction is later found to have been unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction will not be ordered without a bond when plaintiff's right is vague and the defendant might be injured. If injunction issued upon bond and defendant prevails, defendant can sue on the bond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and temporal limits of injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction remains in force as long as the patent is capable of infringement, unless previously recalled by the court or superseded by other judgment in the suit; it must be directed only against devices constructed while the patent was in force and should be limited to the life of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction forbidding use after the patent term effectively extends the patent and is improper. Where the date of expiration is disputed the court will not fix a premature limit but the defendant can move to dissolve when the claimed expiration arrives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and personal scope of injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: An injunction takes effect according to its terms and operates only upon the persons and the actions named therein; it has no authority over acts or individuals beyond the local jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may enjoin sellers' vendees where appropriate (e.g., pending suit against the maker plaintiff may be enjoined from suing vendor's vendees), but jurisdictional and party-nonjoinder limits apply; bonds may be required when asserting influence over parties in other districts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations when plaintiff is patentee or when equity will not interfere
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity will not issue an injunction to restrain a patentee (i.e., a patentee cannot be enjoined in the same manner), and no injunctive relief will be ordered to affect unrelated future litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will not render decisions merely to affect other cases; where plaintiff is patentee the relief sought must comport with established equitable principles and jurisdictional limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when affidavits or evidence are late or when new matters are raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits filed after the stipulated date cannot be considered on a motion for an injunction; where defendant sets up new matter (e.g., license) plaintiff may reply with more proofs, but the defendant cannot put in additional evidence to rebut such proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental bills may add new apprehended infringements discovered after filing and may be covered by same injunction; parties must follow procedural timetables to preserve right to have affidavits considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: When injunctions may be limited to particular claims or devices
rubrics_metrics.description: When certain claims of the patent are disputed, the injunction may be confined to those which are unquestionably valid; when certain infringing devices already used by defendant cannot be equitably enjoined, he may be forbidden to procure others and employ them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction may forbid employment of other devices than those already in use and may enjoin infringement of particular claims even though other claims remain disputed.
